title: Keep clip bounds one-dimensional during operand alignment
answers: Why does DataFrame.clip turn integer columns into object dtype with nullable integer bounds?
Why does inplace clipping fail with an extension-dtype array or Index bound?
What does flex=None mean in DataFrame._align_for_op?
body:
Symptom: DataFrame.clip with an extension-dtype array or Index bound degrades integer columns to object dtype or raises TypeError with inplace=True.
Root cause: pandas/core/frame.py:DataFrame._align_for_op broadcast the aligned Series bound through _maybe_align_series_as_frame; the resulting EA-columned frame bypassed where's working one-dimensional EA path.
Fix pattern: Preserve the aligned Series operand when flex=None so clipping passes a one-dimensional bound to where.
Constraints: flex=None skips DataFrame alignment checks and Series-to-frame broadcasting; keep broadcasting for flex values other than None. This guard is enforced in pandas/core/frame.py:DataFrame._align_for_op.
applies: DataFrame operand alignment used to pass list-like clipping bounds to where, especially extension-dtype arrays and Index objects.
